submission.prose: Implements the typed FSM instance and its factory: it turns a builder definition into independent machines, owns per-instance context/state/queue/timers, executes event lifecycles, and emits optional traces. Definition construction/validation is delegated to the DSL implementation; keyed scheduling to the timer registry; specialized failures to the error module. The repository README describes substantially the same design, but its timer-payload claim conflicts with the captured implementation.

children.prose: `define` runs the caller's builder body, asks `FsmBuilderImpl` to validate and compile it, then returns a closure sharing that immutable-looking definition. Each factory call creates a machine with its own context, initial state, queue, timer registry and trace identity; initial-state entry actions run during construction. The factory type makes context parameters optional only when `Context` is `void`.
qualifications: The definition object is shared by closure; immutability is only apparent from its use and readonly-facing types, not independently enforced here.
Behavior inferred from source without execution.

children.prose: `dispatch` always enqueues. The outermost call synchronously drains FIFO; re-entrant calls return and leave work to that drain. Unknown events fail before lookup. Handling runs state-specific begin actions and first-match transitions, then fallback begins/transitions; defined transitions whose guards all fail count as an implicit stay, while no state/fallback definition raises an unhandled-event error. Any thrown guard/action error clears remaining queued events and propagates.

qualifications: Synchronous and FIFO characterize the visible source algorithm, not measured execution.

children.prose: Transitions are tested in declaration order and all guards on a candidate must pass. Internal transitions run only transition actions. External transitions run old-state exit actions, transition actions, assign the target state, then run target entry actions. Every callback receives the shared context plus typed event/state metadata and a restricted action API; events emitted by callbacks are queued until the current event finishes.
qualifications: Ordering is directly visible in source but was not executed.
An exception during entry occurs after state assignment; earlier transition-stage exceptions occur before assignment.

children.prose: The callback API can redispatch, schedule an event, or cancel one/all timers. `TimerRegistry` owns replacement-by-key, cancellation, relative delays, performance-clock deadlines, immediate clamping of past/negative times, and `Infinity` as unscheduled. The engine also formats optional timestamped traces for events, guards, selected transitions, actions, fallbacks and runtime errors, using a replaceable logger.

inconsistencies.reason: The README says `fsm.timer({ event, ..., payload? })` schedules a future dispatch with that payload. The implementation constructs an empty argument list when `payload` is present and `[params.payload]` when it is absent, so an explicitly supplied payload appears to be dropped; this likely reverses the intended condition.
qualifications: Static source reading only; no timer was executed.
This conflicts with documentation and with the apparent typed action-API intent; whether generated output differs was not investigated.
